name: Elevator and escalator services

problems.words: Breakdown calls come in at night and the on-call technician doesn't pick up
quick_ideas: Give every building a second number to call if the duty technician doesn't answer, so no call dead-ends
Share the night roster with each building, so guards know who is on.

workzap_build.text: A breakdown line that creates a time-stamped ticket and alerts the on-call staff in turn, with entrapments escalated to management within minutes.

problems.ask_first: How many technicians are on call at night?
problems.free_stops: Escalation rules and timings are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each night breakdown call with the time answered or missed, so you can see how often the duty line fails after hours.
Assign one backup dispatcher for night calls and keep the handover note in one place, so missed calls reach a second person quickly.

problems.words: We don't know our average response time to a breakdown
quick_ideas: Record time reported and time arrived for every call this week, so you have a first baseline
Look at the slowest calls, so you see where delay happens.

workzap_build.text: Response and fix times measured on every ticket, by building and technician, updated daily.

problems.ask_first: How do breakdown calls reach you, day and night?
problems.free_stops: KPI definitions and targets are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare reported time and arrival time for each breakdown this week, so your true average delay stops being a guess.
Give one person the job of writing every breakdown start and arrival time in one notebook, so response tracking stays consistent daily.

problems.words: Monthly PM visits are skipped and the client finds out
quick_ideas: Give each technician a written monthly visit list, so every lift has a planned date
Ask for a photo and time from each visit, so completion is provable.

workzap_build.text: A PM scheduler with visit lists, a checklist with photo and time proof, and missed visits flagged every day.

problems.ask_first: How do you confirm a visit actually happened?
problems.free_stops: Scheduling rules are in the solution document; checklist content stays with your engineers.

extra_ideas.text: Walk through this month's PM list and mark which lifts were visited and which were missed, so client surprises are easier to prevent.
Set one fixed afternoon each week to update one shared PM list, so missed visits are caught before the client spots them.

problems.words: Expensive parts are used on non-comprehensive contracts and never billed
quick_ideas: Check last month's parts against each lift's contract type, so missed charges surface
Note the contract type on every parts slip, so it's clear at issue time.

workzap_build.text: A parts issue log linked to each lift that flags chargeable parts by contract type and passes them to billing.

problems.ask_first: How are extra parts billed today?
problems.free_stops: Billing rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare parts issued this week against non-comprehensive jobs completed, so missed billable items are easier to spot before invoicing.
Make one person review every non-comprehensive job slip before filing, so chargeable parts are flagged while the work is still fresh.

problems.words: Inspection certificates for some lifts expired without us noticing
quick_ideas: List every lift's certificate and inspection date in one place, so expiries are visible
Give one person ownership of renewals, so it is never assumed.

workzap_build.text: An asset register for every lift and escalator with certificate and AMC expiry alerts sent well ahead.

problems.ask_first: Who keeps track of inspection due dates?
problems.free_stops: Alert timing is in the solution document; certification rules are for the regulator and licensed inspectors.

extra_ideas.text: Check every lift's latest inspection date against this month's calendar, so upcoming certificate expiries are seen before clients raise them.
Give one admin person a fixed weekly check of all certificate dates in one notebook, so renewals stop slipping between other tasks.

problems.words: Same lift breaks down three times in a month
quick_ideas: List lifts with repeat breakdowns this quarter, so the worst are known
Have a senior technician review each one, so the root cause is looked at.

workzap_build.text: Repeat-breakdown alerts per lift that prompt a root-cause review or a modernisation proposal.

problems.ask_first: How many lifts and escalators are you maintaining?
problems.free_stops: Alert thresholds and review flow are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count repeat breakdown visits by lift for this month, so the worst recurring units stand out for deeper technical review.
Assign one senior technician to own repeat-fault reviews in one shared log, so recurring lift problems get chased to closure.

problems.words: Technicians take parts and we can't trace which lift they went into
quick_ideas: Write the lift reference on every parts slip, so each part has a destination
Check high-value parts against slips weekly.

workzap_build.text: Parts issued against a specific lift, with stock levels and slow-to-source items flagged.

problems.ask_first: Which parts are hardest to get?
problems.free_stops: Parts tracking design is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare parts taken from stores with jobs closed this week, so missing lift references on used items are easy to spot.
Keep one issue notebook at the stores desk with one person checking entries daily, so each part leaves with a clear lift destination.

problems.words: Clients want monthly reports and we prepare them by hand
quick_ideas: Fix one report layout for all buildings, so it's built the same way
Collect visit and breakdown data weekly, so month-end isn't a scramble.

workzap_build.text: Monthly client reports generated per building from tickets and visits.

problems.ask_first: What do building managers ask for every month?
problems.free_stops: Report content is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which monthly report details are chased at month end, so you see exactly what information was not captured during the month.
Give one admin person a fixed weekly slot to gather visit and breakdown notes into one file, so month-end report prep is lighter.

problems.words: Building managers pay AMC invoices months late
quick_ideas: List unpaid invoices by building and age, so the oldest are clear
Attach the month's visit summary to each invoice, so proof travels with the bill.

workzap_build.text: AMC billing and receivables per building with reminders on schedule.

problems.free_stops: Reminder schedule is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many AMC invoices went out without a same month visit note attached, so missing proof behind delays becomes visible.
Keep one notebook page for sent invoices and attached visit notes, so staff can spot missing paperwork before bills leave.

problems.words: Modernisation quotes go out and we never follow up
quick_ideas: List open quotes with the date sent, so ageing is visible
Give each quote a follow-up owner, so none is forgotten.

workzap_build.text: A modernisation and installation quote pipeline with follow-up reminders.

problems.ask_first: How many quotes are open right now?
problems.free_stops: Pipeline stages are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count open modernisation quotes by weeks since sent, so you see which proposals have gone cold the longest.
Give one staff member a fixed weekly follow-up hour and one notebook page for all open quotes, so no proposal sits untouched.

never_say: Any rescue, override, brake release or manual-move instructions, even for a technician.
Any safety or compliance judgement; licensed inspectors and engineers decide.
Any help issuing certificates without inspection, backdating PM records, bypassing safety devices or bribing inspectors.
Any recording of trapped people's, residents', client contacts' or technicians' names.
Anything other than emergency services first for an entrapment, injury, shaft fall, smoke or fire.

sample_reply.person: What can we do about night breakdown calls? We maintain about 300 lifts and the duty technician doesn't always answer.
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, there is a way through this, and the first steps are simple.
First, give every building a second number to call when the duty technician doesn't answer, so no call dead-ends.
Second, share the night roster with each building so guards know who is on.
Here is what Workzap would build: every call time-stamped as a ticket and escalated up the roster if nobody picks up.

Shall I prepare a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
